body: This test mutates the curve after `set_point_count(3)` by re-setting `point_0/position` and `point_1/position` from cached values, which makes it incapable of catching regressions where expanding the point array changes/remaps existing indexed properties. To actually verify preservation, remove the `set(...)` calls and assert that `curve->get(\"point_0/position\")`/`curve->get_point_position(0)` (and index 1) are unchanged immediately after `set_point_count(3)`.

Replacing `_add_point(Vector2())` with a raw `_points.push_back(Point(...))` risks bypassing any invariants `_add_point` enforces (e.g., tangent/handle modes, per-point metadata, sorting/normalization, or ensuring neighboring points’ tangents are updated). This can lead to behavioral differences vs the prior code path beyond just the default position. Prefer calling `_add_point(Vector2(default_offset, default_value))` (or introducing/using a helper that adds a point with a specific position) so point initialization and tangent updates stay consistent.

The `old_size > 0` branch uses `_max_domain` without clamping, while the `old_size == 0` branch clamps a literal `0.0`. To keep the behavior uniform and robust against future domain changes, clamp `_max_domain` as well (or compute the default from the last point’s offset/value if the intent is to append ‘at the end’ of the current curve). This makes the default-point placement logic easier to reason about and reduces surprises.

This is setting the property value to the previous one and then checks if it's correct.
Seems weird to me, the property check could be a separate test. For the purpose of testing point index after expanding, the test case could end on the checks above.
